papers.ai_note: 摘要已自行承认核酸检测量与监测条件改变使跨波峰值比较不可靠，10.7–99.9%的降幅区间极宽、异质性大，不宜作疗效性解读。哨点监测的早期预警假设为阴性结果（滞后交叉相关显示同步而非领先），作者结论口径与之一致，但研究属生态学时序相关，无法排除指标同步受共同外部驱动（政策、就诊行为）影响；无个体层级数据、无混杂控制，属方法学局限。信息不足：各指标绝对数值、样本量与变异株检测覆盖面。
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Using Fujian's multi-source Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) surveillance system, this study compared epidemiological features and indicator associations of two successive epidemic waves to optimize epidemic surveillance and prevention strategies. METHODS: Multi-source surveillance data were collected from week 49 of 2022 (the week of December 7, 2022, when the 10 optimization measures were issued) to week 29 of 2023 (July 17-23, 2023) in Fujian Province, including reported COVID-19 cases, fever clinic visits, population nucleic acid testing, sentinel hospital surveillance, hospitalized severe cases, and viral variants. Descriptive epidemiology, Spearman correlation, and lagged cross-correlation analyses were adopted for data evaluation. RESULTS: The first wave showed a sharp peak pattern, with most indicators peaking around weeks 51-52/2022 and reported cases peaking at week 1/2023; the second wave exhibited a gradual peak at week 21/2023. Peak levels of the second wave were 10.7-99.9% lower across indicators, although the markedly reduced nucleic acid testing volume and changed surveillance conditions warrant cautious interpretation of cross-wave comparisons. The interval between the two epidemic peaks was about 5 months, and severe cases consistently lagged infection peaks by approximately 2 weeks. Indicators were strongly correlated, with the highest correlation between sentinel and nucleic acid positivity rates (rs = 0.92, p < 0.001); lagged cross-correlation analysis indicated that these two indicators moved essentially in synchrony. The XBB variant took approximately 4 weeks from initial local detection to predominance alongside the second epidemic peak. CONCLUSION: The two observed epidemic peaks were approximately 5 months apart, and multi-source surveillance indicators showed high temporal concordance. However, lagged cross-correlation indicated that the indicators moved essentially in synchrony, so sentinel surveillance should be regarded as a complementary monitoring tool rather than a proven early-warning measure. The XBB variant reached predominance approximately 4 weeks after initial local detection in this episode, a descriptive observation that cannot be generalized as a validated predictive tool. These findings facilitate multi-wave epidemic preparedness and surveillance improvement.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Co-infection can accelerate the progression of SFTS, this study aims to analyze the clinical characteristics of SFTS-associated co-infection and identify the associated risk factors. METHODS: In this retrospective study, we analyzed epidemiology, pathogen distribution patterns, and laboratory findings between community-acquired infections (CAIs) and hospital-acquired infections (HAIs) in SFTS patients. Our objectives were to determine the prevalence, characterize clinical manifestations, and identify potential risk factors associated with SFTS co-infection. RESULTS: Among 231 SFTS patients, 81 (35.1%) had co-infection. SFTS patients with CAIs exhibited the highest mortality rate (23.4%). Compared to those without co-infection, patients with CAIs had more severe clinical presentation and poorer outcome. Antifungal treatment significantly improved survival in SFTS with CAIs-related fungal infections, but had no benefit in those with HAIs-related fungal infections. Pulmonary infections were associated with reduced survival time in SFTS patients with HAIs but had no significant impact on those with CAIs. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified several independent risk factors for CAIs in SFTS patients, including diarrhea, cerebral infarction, antifungal therapy, ICU admission, elevated D-Dimer levels, and A/G <1.05. Among SFTS patients with co-infection, A/G <1.05 demonstrated potential predictive value for CAIs (AUC = 0.714, 95% CI: 0.626-0.832). Further analysis revealed that an A/G ratio <1.05 indicated moderate discriminatory performance for SFTS patients with CAIs related pulmonary fungal infections (AUC = 0.799, 95% CI: 0.702-0.896). CONCLUSIONS: SFTS patients with CAIs had poorer clinical outcomes than patients without co-infection or those with HAIs. An A/G ratio <1.05 may serve as a supportive marker for identifying patients at increased risk of CAIs and could assist clinical risk stratification.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) at admission and 14-day adverse clinical outcomes in patients with pyogenic liver abscess (PLA), and to evaluate its discriminatory performance. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 670 adults with PLA admitted to Linyi People's Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. SIRI was calculated from the first complete blood count obtained within 24 hours after admission according to the study data-collection criteria. The primary outcome was a composite of adverse clinical events within 14 days. A base logistic regression model and a model additionally including SIRI were fitted in 30 multiply imputed datasets, with complete-case and death-exclusion sensitivity analyses. Restricted cubic splines, receiver operating characteristic curves, and exploratory measures of incremental performance were evaluated. RESULTS: Of the 670 patients, 100 (14.9%) experienced an adverse clinical outcome, including four deaths. Median SIRI was higher in patients with adverse outcomes [8.95 (4.14-15.64) vs. 5.80 (2.93-11.64); P< 0.001]. In the multiply imputed linear model, the adjusted OR for SIRI was 1.0187 (95% CI, 1.0022-1.0354; P = 0.0262); the complete-case estimate was 1.0163 (95% CI, 0.9994-1.0334; P = 0.0588). After exclusion of four deaths, the adjusted OR was 1.0191 (95% CI, 1.0026-1.0360; P = 0.0233) among 666 patients with 96 nonfatal adverse outcomes. The spline overall association and nonlinearity P values were 0.0557 and 0.4080, respectively. The AUC for SIRI was 0.6072, lower than that for NLR (0.6782; paired DeLong P = 0.0015). Adding SIRI increased the apparent model AUC by 0.0116 (95% bootstrap interval, -0.0006 to 0.0351). CONCLUSION: Higher admission SIRI was associated with greater odds of 14-day adverse clinical outcomes in the multiply imputed linear model, but its standalone discrimination was limited. Sensitivity analyses and incremental performance estimates indicate uncertainty, and clinical utility requires further validation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Individuals on opioids are found dead in bed and respiratory depression is a potential cause. In contrast to other opioids, buprenorphine, a partial μ-opioid receptor agonist has reduced respiratory depression. However, death has also been reported in individuals using buprenorphine; yet, it is not known if chronic use of buprenorphine could be associated with clinically significant respiratory depression. OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this preliminary study was to determine if chronic buprenorphine use is associated with sleep disordered breathing. METHODS: A retrospective study of 11 consecutive patients who were using buprenorphine chronically and referred for sleep evaluation. All underwent full night attended polysomnography and polysomnograms were scored page by page by a board-certified sleep physician. RESULTS: Two breathing patterns were observed. First, four patients had central sleep apnea (CSA) with an index of ≥5/h of sleep and an average of 13. When compared to those without CSA, patients with CSA suffered from severe sleep apnea with an apnea hypopnea index (AHI) of 35 (vs.9/hour of sleep) and associated with clinically significant low saturation (75% vs. 87%). Second, the group without significant CSA (CAI <5, n = 7), despite a low AHI, had relatively more sustained desaturation time below 90% (91 vs 51 min), suggesting hypoventilation. CONCLUSIONS: Despite improved respiratory safety profile, this preliminary study is the first to provide evidence that chronic use of buprenorphine is associated with clinically significant sleep disorders with two distinct patterns shared with other opioids. These disordered breathing events could be a potential cause of buprenorphine-associated death reported in the literature, a finding also shared with other opioids. Clinicians should be aware of this association.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Human patient-derived oesophageal epithelial models are limited, and organoid cultures often have short passaging lifespans, restricting studies of tissue homeostasis and disease. We aimed to establish and characterise primary oesophageal organoids from non-pathologic epithelium as a renewable epithelial source and adaptable modelling platform. METHODS: Primary oesophageal tissues were obtained from endoscopic biopsies and surgical resections. Basal epithelial cells were isolated and cultured under optimised conditions to establish long-term three-dimensional organoids. Organoid-derived cells were expanded as two-dimensional monolayers and re-seeded into 3D culture. Epithelial identity and differentiation were assessed by immunostaining and RT-qPCR (reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction) analysis of markers. RESULTS: Primary organoids were established and maintained while preserving epithelial markers. Expression of KRT14, involucrin, loricrin and filaggrin confirmed the oesophageal phenotype. Larger, multilayered primary organoids showed increased expression of differentiation-associated markers relative to 2D monolayers and re-seeded small organoids, indicating culture configuration influences epithelial differentiation while maintaining lineage identity. CONCLUSIONS: We established a robust and reproducible protocol for generating and maintaining oesophageal organoids across culture formats. These models retained epithelial features while exhibiting culture-dependent differentiation. This platform enables complementary 2D and 3D investigation of oesophageal epithelial biology and supports future comparison of healthy and disease-derived tissues for patient-specific modelling and mechanistic studies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Post-COVID Condition (PCC) is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome in which chronic fatigue and functional limitation are among the most disabling manifestations. Alterations in the gut microbiota have been proposed as contributors to PCC pathophysiology; however, it remains unclear whether distinct clinical PCC phenotypes are associated with specific microbiota signatures. RESULTS: This cross-sectional pilot study analysed gut microbiota composition and predicted functional capacity in 50 participants from Aragón (Spain), including 30 patients with PCC and 20 healthy controls. PCC patients were stratified according to the presence of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS)-like symptoms and functional limitation assessed using the 6-Minute Walking Test. Alpha and beta diversity did not differ significantly between groups (Figs. 2 and 3). Differential abundance analysis identified taxon-level differences between groups. Escherichia/Shigella was enriched in PCC-CFS relative to controls, both overall and in the subgroup without functional limitation, representing the most consistent signal. Additional differences included higher Streptococcus and Veillonella in controls, and higher Flavonifractor and Hungatella in PCC-NCFS. After adjustment for digestive symptoms and vaccine dose, these associations attenuated and none remained significant, indicating that they may be partly driven by confounding.PICRUSt2 functional predictions suggested differences in pathways related to nucleotide and amino acid metabolism; however, none remained significant after correction for multiple testing and should therefore be considered exploratory. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest the presence of phenotype-associated taxonomic differences within PCC despite the absence of global diversity alterations. The results should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating due to the limited subgroup sample sizes. Larger studies incorporating metagenomic and metabolomic approaches are needed to validate these observations and clarify their potential clinical relevance.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgery, Montefiore Medical Center and Albert Einstein College of Medicine, Br…

papers.abstract_en: Stage II to III NSCLC management is an evolving field with several multimodal treatment strategies. Management decisions are dictated by disease stage, resectability, biomarker testing, and resource availability, along with patient factors and preferences. To optimize outcomes for patients with stage II to III NSCLC, early and accurate diagnosis and staging, molecular alteration assessment, and evaluation of resectability and operability are essential to support a personalized treatment approach. To best facilitate comprehensive NSCLC care, a multidisciplinary team (MDT) composed of different healthcare specialists is critical. Here, we review MDT care in stage II to III NSCLC management and the benefits it provides to patients, including accurate staging, compliance with molecular testing, reduced time to treatment initiation, greater adherence to treatment guidelines, enhanced health system efficiencies, and ultimately improved outcomes. Despite these benefits, many patients do not have access to MDT care, or it is not well implemented. We review the barriers to MDT care, ranging from limited access to diagnostic technologies and specialists, costs, best practices and incentives, clinical pathway limitations, and racial and socioeconomic disparities, and provide recommendations to address these barriers. These include the development of regional MDTs and triage systems, along with incentivizing MDT care and standardizing best practices and workflows. We further discuss advances in stage II to III NSCLC, including the continuing evolution of diagnostics, treatment strategies, and artificial intelligence-based management algorithms, where MDTs must be able to adapt to incorporate these innovations.

papers.authors: Mazzone S, Birring SS, Gibson PG, Song WJ
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Anatomy and Physiology, University of Melbourne, Melbourne, VIC, Australia.
papers.authors_conclusion: We introduce the Neuroanatomic Diagnostic Protocol and the rationale behind it, a proposed timely and practical update to the classic framework that unifies the known association of cough with common etiological causes, the existence of refractory chronic cough, and the core concepts of cough hypersensitivity syndrome by acknowledging the vagus nerve and its central circuits as a distinct anatomical consideration in the effective assessment and targeted management of chronic cough.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic cough represents a challenging clinical problem and significant unmet global burden. For some patients, cough can be associated with conditions impacting the respiratory system, including asthma, rhinosinusitis, and gastroesophageal reflux disease. This underpinned the rationale for the development of the Anatomic Diagnostic Protocol, an etiology-based algorithm for chronic cough management used in clinical practice for over 50 years. However, despite the value of the Anatomic Diagnostic Protocol, many patients do not respond adequately to the clinical strategies promoted in the existing management framework because they either have no obvious causative disease or their cough is unresolved by standard etiology-based therapies (refractory chronic cough). This, along with the introduction of cough hypersensitivity syndrome as a unifying condition common to most patients with chronic cough, has added additional complexity for physicians in everyday practice. FINDINGS: We introduce the Neuroanatomic Diagnostic Protocol and the rationale behind it, a proposed timely and practical update to the classic framework that unifies the known association of cough with common etiological causes, the existence of refractory chronic cough, and the core concepts of cough hypersensitivity syndrome by acknowledging the vagus nerve and its central circuits as a distinct anatomical consideration in the effective assessment and targeted management of chronic cough.

papers.abstract_en: This study aimed to characterize and compare methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strains isolated from community members and healthcare workers (HCWs) in Egypt using antibiotic susceptibility testing, mecA gene detection, SCCmec typing, and ERIC-PCR fingerprinting. A cross-sectional study was conducted between September 2024 and January 2025, during which 450 specimens were collected from Mansoura University Hospitals and the local community, where 71 specimens (30.8%) were confirmed as MRSA. MRSA prevalence was significantly higher among HCWs, 62.5% (50/80), than among community members, 14% (21/150). In general, antibiotic resistance rates were higher in HCW strains. All isolates were resistant to cefoxitin and sensitive to vancomycin.The methicillin-resistant phenotype of the 71 MRSA isolates was confirmed by positive mecA gene tests, with SCCmec Type III prevalent among healthcare workers and SCCmec Type IV predominating in the community. ERIC-PCR fingerprinting demonstrated the isolates' genetic diversity. The dendrogram based on ERIC patterns showed distinct clusters between community and hospital strains, though with some overlap, suggesting possible transmission between the two populations.In conclusion, MRSA strains from HCWs displayed broader antibiotic resistance and greater clonal similarity, while community strains were more diverse and less resistant. The presence of intermixed clusters between community-acquired (CA-MRSA) and (HCW-MRSA) suggested a possible bidirectional transmission pathway, underscoring the blurring of epidemiological boundaries.These results underline the necessity of ongoing molecular surveillance and integrated infection control strategies to track the spread of MRSA in community and clinical settings.

papers.abstract_en: Halophilic archaea are a distinct domain of life, separate from Bacteria and Eukarya, that thrive in highly saline environments, including salt mines. Their impact on the human immune system is poorly known. The respiratory epithelium is the first line of defence against inhaled environmental agents, including pollutants, allergens and microorganisms. Disruption of epithelial barrier integrity is linked to the pathogenesis of allergic and inflammatory airway diseases. In this study we examined the interaction of Halorhabdus rudnickae WSM-64T, isolated from the Barycz area of the Wieliczka Salt-Mine in Poland with the human bronchial epithelial cell line Calu-3. We found that this halophilic archaeal strain did not cause cytotoxic or genotoxic effects on Calu-3 cells and significantly enhanced the healing process of physically damaged monolayers of cells compared to unstimulated cells. Moreover, halophilic archaeal stimulation of Calu-3 was associated with significantly increased fluorescence intensity of ZO-1, scaffolding protein responsible for organizing the junctional proteins and stabilising cell barriers. Exposure to Hrd. rudnickae significantly decreased the secretion of TGF-beta by Calu-3 cells, suggesting a potential ability to counteract the pathological changes driven by TGF-beta. In the air-liquid interface model we observed significant reduction in FITC-dextran permeability, indicating improved barrier integrity after stimulation of Calu-3 with halophilic archaea. Our findings thus show that halophilic archaeon Hrd. rudnickae isolated from a Polish salt mine can induce the enhancement of epithelial barrier integrity in the Calu-3 cells, providing a conceptual framework for future immunomodulatory strategies in patients with pulmonary allergic disorders.

papers.abstract_en: Staphylococcus aureus(S. aureus)is an important foodborne pathogen. Host-derived catecholamines released under stress are known to influence bacterial pathogenic processes, including growth, virulence, biofilm formation. However, the role of dopamine in this context remains less well understood, particularly in S. aureus. In this study, we investigated the effects of dopamine on S. aureus ATCC 25,923 using a combination of phenotypic assays and multi-omics analyses. Dopamine was taken up by the bacteria and was associated with enhanced pathogenic phenotypes, including increased proliferation, toxin production, biofilm formation, motility, adhesion, and multidrug resistance. In a mouse infection experiment, dopamine treatment further increased bacterial colonization and organ invasion. Mechanistically, multi-omics analyses indicated that dopamine activates the SaeRS two-component system and is associated with the upregulation of virulence-related factors, adhesion-associated proteins, and membrane lipid synthesis pathways, along with increased activity in key metabolic processes such as the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle and oxidative phosphorylation. Importantly, deletion of saeS markedly attenuated these dopamine-associated effects. Taken together, these findings suggest that dopamine likely influences S. aureus pathogenicity primarily through the SaeRS signaling pathway and provide insight into how host stress signals may contribute to bacterial infection.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The systemic and relapsing nature of urticaria cannot be fully explained by cutaneous mast-cell activation alone. Whether the gut contributes, and whether a multi-component formula such as Jingfang Mixture (JF) acts through a gut-skin route, have not been tested together at the level of microbiota, metabolites, and skin signaling together. METHODS: Using an OVA (ovalbumin)/Al(OH)3-induced urticaria-like allergic inflammation rat model, we integrated 16S rRNA gene sequencing, fecal untargeted metabolomics, and skin DIA (data-independent acquisition)-based quantitative proteomics to investigate the therapeutic mechanisms of JF. RESULTS: JF suppressed both Th2 (IgE (immunoglobulin E), IL-4 (interleukin-4)) and Th17/pro-inflammatory (IL-6 (interleukin-6), TNF-α (tumor necrosis factor-α), IL-17 (interleukin-17)) responses, improved intestinal barrier-associated abnormalities, and partially reversed gut dysbiosis by restoring SCFA-producing bacteria (Bacteroidia, Clostridia, Lachnospirales, Oscillospirales) while reducing Proteobacteria and Enterobacterales. JF normalized the fecal metabolome, elevating anti-inflammatory metabolites including butyrate, indole, indole-3-acetic acid, docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) and reducing pro-inflammatory mediators such as arachidonic acid, leukotriene B4, secondary bile acids. At the skin level, JF activated AMPK (AMP-activated protein kinase) signaling and suppressed aberrant p38 MAPK (p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase) and PI3K (phosphoinositide 3-kinase)-Akt (protein kinase B) activation. Spearman correlation analysis further revealed that SCFAs (short-chain fatty acids) and indole derivatives were positively correlated with the abundance of AMPK-pathway-related proteins and negatively with p38 MAPK and PI3K-Akt proteins, whereas pro-inflammatory metabolites exhibited inverse correlation patterns. CONCLUSION: Collectively, our findings indicate that JF mitigates urticaria-like inflammation, likely through gut microbiota and modulating SCFA, bile acid, tryptophan, and lipid metabolism. This multi-omics evidence suggests that JF may act through the gut microbiota-metabolite-skin signaling axis to confer anti-urticarial benefits. Nevertheless, further causal validation experiments and clinical investigations are warranted.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUNDS: Hyperuricemia (HUA) has become a global health issue due to its rapidly increasing prevalence. Growing evidence from population and animal studies suggests that gut microbial dysbiosis and lifestyle changes are involved in serum uric acid metabolism. However, most existing studies are limited by small sample sizes or have yielded inconsistent findings. This study aimed to jointly investigate the associations of the gut microbiome, lifestyles, and dietary habits with HUA in Chinese elderly adults. METHODS: A community-based case-control study was conducted across nine provincial-level regions in China, involving 617 participants. Data collection included lifestyle and dietary habit questionnaires, chronic disease history, serum uric acid (sUA) measurement, and 16S rRNA sequencing of fecal samples. RESULTS: Taxonomic composition and diversity analyses revealed significant difference between the HUA and controls in gut microbiota structure and diversity. Through differential abundance and co-occurrence network analyses, 42 microbial signatures associated with HUA or sUA were identified. Notably, the prevalence of g_Stenotrophomonas was positively associated with short sleep duration. A microbial risk score (MRS) model constructed using these signatures demonstrated an area under curve (AUC) of 0.761 in the discovery cohort and 0.675 in the validation cohort. Furthermore, a significant positive association was observed between sleep quality (sleep duration, number of awakenings, and short sleep duration) and the MRS model. CONCLUSIONS: These results add to the accumulating evidence implicating the role of gut microbiota and sleep in HUA, such as g_Stenotrophomonas, and inform the potential effect of the microbiome-based association between sleep duration and HUA. However, due to the cross-sectional design, we cannot infer causality from these associations, and the observed findings should be confirmed in prospective studies.

papers.abstract_en: Recurrent pulmonary infection (RPI) refers to the frequent and repeated episodes of lower respiratory tract infections. At its core, it represents a vicious cycle arising from the disruption of the homeostatic balance among pathogens, host immunity, and pulmonary architecture. RPI accounts for a considerable proportion of pediatric pneumonia cases, and the cumulative incidence among elderly patients hospitalized for pneumonia is also markedly elevated, imposing a substantial disease burden. The etiologies are notably diverse, beyond common pathogens such as bacteria and viruses, the ubiquity of asymptomatic colonization, underlying comorbidities, immune deficiencies, medication-related factors, and aspiration all constitute critical predisposing factors. This review summarizes the pathogenic characteristics of RPI, host-related factors, and the mechanistic roles of structural lung damage in infection recurrence. It further focuses on the current advances and limitations of precision diagnostic approaches (metagenomic sequencing), immunomodulatory and microbiome-targeted interventions, and vaccination strategies. Existing evidence suggests that the clinical benefits of these interventions in RPI remain to be validated by more high-quality studies. The aim of this article is to provide a reference for the clinical management of RPI and to inform future research directions.

papers.abstract_en: Oral biofilms are spatially ordered microbial communities whose pathogenic behavior is shaped by more than taxonomic composition. Their development reflects the combined effects of adhesin-receptor recognition, interspecies coaggregation, matrix formation, metabolite exchange, local physicochemical gradients and host-derived selection. Here, we synthesize molecular and ecological evidence on the bacterial cell surface-matrix interface and consider how these interactions contribute to cariogenic, periodontal and peri-implant biofilms. Particular attention is given to glucosyltransferase-dependent polysaccharides, extracellular DNA, amyloidogenic proteins, sortase-anchored surface factors and outer membrane vesicles, together with metabolic interactions involving lactate, arginine, hydrogen peroxide and heme. We further evaluate functional-genomic and systems-level approaches (including transposon sequencing, CRISPR interference, metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, metaproteomics, metabolomics, spatial imaging, genome-scale metabolic modeling and machine learning) while distinguishing association and prediction from experimentally demonstrated mechanism. Emerging interventions are assessed according to their biological target and evidence level, including adhesion blockade, specifically targeted antimicrobials, matrix synthesis inhibition and degradation, quorum interference, probiotics, catalytic nanoparticles, antimicrobial photodynamic therapy and antibiofilm dental materials. Across these approaches, reduction in biofilm biomass is not equivalent to ecological restoration or clinical benefit. Key translational barriers include model fidelity, donor-to-donor variation, spatial heterogeneity, treatment durability, endpoint selection and the limited external validation of many computational and preclinical findings. Future precision strategies should therefore integrate microbial identity, matrix architecture, spatial metabolism and host context, with experimental perturbation used to establish causal vulnerabilities before therapeutic translation.

papers.abstract_en: Bandavirus dabieense (DBV), the causative agent of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), is an emerging tick-borne pathogen associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Despite increasing incidence across East and Southeast Asia, the pathogenic mechanisms of DBV infection remain incompletely understood, and no specific antiviral therapies have been approved. Robust preclinical models are therefore essential for elucidating viral pathogenesis and accelerating therapeutic and vaccine development. In this Review, we summarize recent advances in cellular and animal models of DBV infection, including established cell lines, primary cells, interferon-deficient rodents, hamsters, ferrets, companion animals, and non-human primates. We critically evaluate the strengths and limitations of these systems in recapitulating key features of human disease and discuss their utility for investigating viral replication, host responses, inflammatory injury, and antiviral efficacy. We further highlight major gaps in the current model landscape and propose priorities for improving the physiological relevance and translational value of DBV experimental systems.

papers.abstract_en: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection, affecting half of the world's population, is the principal cause of peptic ulcer disease and gastric cancer, yet its clinical management is increasingly undermined by the rapidly escalating global burden of antibiotic resistance, the suboptimal accuracy of conventional diagnostic methods, and the declining efficacy of empirical therapeutic regimens. Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping this landscape, but existing research remains fragmented across single modalities. We propose a conceptual five-module framework that integrates AI approaches across the H. pylori care continuum: (1) global disease burden and the evolutionary dynamics of H. pylori drug resistance; (2) the application of multimodal AI, from convolutional neural networks to vision-language foundation models, for endoscopic early screening, pathological identification, and functional assessment; (3) the harnessing of machine learning (ML) on genomic and electronic health record data to decipher resistance mechanisms and generate personalized eradication regimens; (4) AI-driven vaccine target discovery and generative design, spanning reverse vaccinology to de novo immunogen creation; and (5) a digital closed-loop patient management platform that leverages new media and reinforcement learning to enhance adherence and eradication rates. We further delineate the core challenges of data bias, cross-scenario generalization, and the critical absence of prospective randomized evidence, and propose a future direction anchored in multimodal foundation models, federated learning, and continuous AI quality improvement. Rather than an established clinical pathway, this framework is proposed as a conceptual blueprint that, once prospectively validated, could upgrade AI-enabled H. pylori care from isolated image recognition toward an end-to-end "perception-reasoning-intervention" system, offering a blueprint for precision prevention and control.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Non-typhoidal Salmonella (NTS) is a leading foodborne pathogen causing severe gastrointestinal and systemic infections, posing a significant global health burden. This study employed a genomic approach to investigate the functional and distribution characteristics of human pathogenome in NTS, aiming to provide molecular targets and a theoretical foundation for novel anti-salmonellosis strategies. RESULTS: Analysis of eight NTS strains revealed 2,000 virulence genes encoding 263 factors, predominantly effector delivery systems (41%), of which type III secretion system (T3SS) genes constituted the majority (66.3%). A total of 217 partial sequences from 13 salmonella pathogenicity islands (SPIs) were identified, with SPI-2 (26.7%), SPI-1 (24%), and SPI-13 (10.6%) being most prevalent. Key virulence genes in SPI-1 (35 T3SS1-related genes), SPI-2 (30 T3SS2-related genes), and SPI-5 (sopB/sigD, pipB) were conserved across all strains. We identified 7,868 human pathogenicity-related genes, functionally enriched in metabolic/cellular processes, catalytic activity, and binding. Human pathogenicity-related virulence genes were mainly classified as delivery systems, adhesion factors, and nutrient metabolism factors. Enzymatic analysis showed human pathogenicity-related protease genes were primarily serine, cysteine, and metallopeptidases, while human pathogenicity-related carbohydrase-active genes were associated with glycoside hydrolases, glycosyltransferases, and carbohydrate esterases. Functional annotation with the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes indicated human pathogenicity-related protease genes enrichment in signaling, cellular, metabolic, and genetic information processing pathways, particularly in antibiotic resistance and infectious diseases, while human pathogenicity-related carbohydrase-active genes were enriched in carbohydrate metabolism and glycan biosynthesis. A structurally conserved, metal-chelating non-ribosomal peptide metallophore (NRP-metallophore) gene cluster was present in all strains, containing biosynthetic virulence genes (entA, entC, entF, entB, entE, fes) and transport-related virulence genes (fep family, entS). Functional type I-E clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) and CRISPR-associated (Cas) systems with variable numbers of CRISPR arrays but conserved direct repeats were identified in most strains. CONCLUSIONS: NTS strains carried conserved T3SS effectors, human pathogenicity-related factors enriched in metabolism, catalysis, antibiotic resistance, and infection pathways, a conserved NRP-metallophore gene cluster for iron acquisition, and a functional type I-E CRISPR-Cas system, collectively defining key genetic determinants for pathogenesis.

papers.abstract_en: Wild Chinese pangolins ingest soil and nest-associated materials while feeding on ants and termites, but these materials are generally absent from captive diets. We assessed whether termitarium soil supplementation was associated with changes in fecal bacterial communities and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) profiles in captive Chinese pangolins. Four adults participated in a sequential within-subject trial comprising a basal diet, a basal diet supplemented with sterilized termitarium soil, and a basal diet supplemented with unsterilized termitarium soil. Fecal bacterial communities were characterized by 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and SCFAs were quantified by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. Community composition differed across dietary stages, whereas alpha diversity did not. At the genus level, Bacteroides abundance was lower during the sterilized-soil stage, whereas Burkholderia-Caballeronia-Paraburkholderia abundance was higher during the unsterilized-soil stage than during the basal-diet stage. Relative to the basal-diet stage, both soil-supplemented stages had lower fecal concentrations of acetate, propionate, butyrate, and valerate. Partial redundancy analysis showed an overall association between the SCFA profile and the selected bacterial genera. PICRUSt2-based predictions also differed across dietary stages, particularly for Xenobiotics Biodegradation and Metabolism. Overall, termitarium soil supplementation was associated with variation in fecal bacterial composition, SCFA concentrations, and predicted functional potential in captive Chinese pangolins. These findings provide a basis for further research on the role of soil-associated materials in the dietary management of captive pangolins.
